input_contract.description: A list of 2-1000 integers, each between 1 and 1000. Order-insensitive: only the minimum and maximum participate.

mutants.description: folds gcd across the whole list
uses nums[0] and nums[-1] instead of min and max
returns min(nums) rather than a divisor
sorts and uses the second element as the minimum
EQUIVALENT: gcd(max, min) rather than gcd(min, max)
mutants.equivalence_argument: gcd is commutative: the set of common divisors of {a, b} does not depend on the order of the pair, so gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a) for all non-negative integers. math.gcd implements the mathematical function, so swapping the operands cannot change the result on any input.

t1-first-and-last-element.why_wrong: A learner who assumes the list arrives sorted takes the ends as the extremes. The specification says explicitly that the list may be in any order.

t1-gcd-of-every-element.why_wrong: The specification's load-bearing sentence is that EXACTLY TWO values participate and every other element is ignored. 'Greatest common divisor of array' reads as the gcd of all of it, and that is what most learners will write.

t1-lcm-instead-of-gcd.why_wrong: gcd and lcm are the pair a learner most often swaps, and both are one call away in math.

t1-returns-the-smallest-value.why_wrong: Confuses 'greatest common divisor of the smallest and largest' with 'the smallest'. Correct whenever the minimum divides the maximum, which is common in small hand-written examples.

t1-second-smallest-and-largest.why_wrong: An off-by-one after sorting — sorted(nums)[1] instead of [0] — which a learner writes when they are mentally skipping a sentinel.
